title: Best Finch Alternatives for Medical Record Retrieval in 2026
summary: Comparing Finch alternatives for medical record retrieval? See how Codes Health, LlamaLab, Tavrn, and others compare on completeness, AI analysis, integrations, and pricing.
body_markdown:
When you're weighing Finch alternatives, the real questions come down to retrieval speed, record completeness, AI capabilities, and how well a service fits your existing workflow. Finch Legal has built a name as a managed pre-litigation service, but plenty of personal injury and plaintiff firms want something different: deeper medical analysis, records checked for completeness, and tight case management integration, all without handing over operational control. This guide walks through six Finch alternatives worth a look, with a close focus on how[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) turns medical record retrieval into a litigation advantage through AI-powered analysis that flags potential breaches of care, treatment gaps, and documented future medical expenses for attorney review.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Codes Health stands out as a strong Finch alternative, pairing retrieval in a couple of weeks with completeness checks and human-reviewed AI insights built for plaintiff litigation


-


Same-day speed isn't the same as a complete record set. Codes Health's position is that same-day services often return only what's immediately available, which pulls clients back into the process and can contribute to churn


-


General AI platforms like ChatGPT aren't designed for litigation-grade medical record review, so test any analysis tool on representative case files and verify its findings


-


Integration options vary: Codes Health offers an embedded Filevine workflow plus custom integrations for high-volume firms, while other providers support their own integrations or work inside a firm's existing system


-


Flat-fee pricing gives Codes Health clients a predictable starting point, though firms should confirm included services and applicable provider charges


-


Missing-record detection can help teams identify documentation gaps before preparing a demand


-


Several alternatives also offer chronologies, summaries, or AI-assisted analysis, so compare specific outputs and review processes rather than assuming a vendor delivers documents only


## **What is Finch Legal and Why Firms Seek Alternatives**


Finch Legal positions itself as a managed pre-litigation service that handles everything from intake through demand drafting. The platform assigns dedicated case managers who monitor client treatment and manage record retrieval as part of a comprehensive operational package.


**Finch Legal Service Model:**


-


24/7 bilingual intake services with automatic CMS updates


-


Dedicated case managers who own files and contact clients every two weeks


-


Medical record retrieval with a reported median turnaround of approximately 14 days


-


Demand package preparation with narratives reviewed by health professionals


-


Treatment monitoring throughout the pre-litigation phase


**Common Reasons Firms Evaluate Alternatives:**


-


**Operational control preferences** : Some firms prefer to retain direct case management rather than delegating to external staff


-


**Specialized medical analysis needs** : Firms handling complex medical malpractice or multi-injury cases may want deeper AI-powered insights


-


**Integration requirements** : Firms with established Filevine workflows should compare embedded integrations with services that operate through staff access to their existing system


-


**Pricing structure alignment** : Bundled service pricing may not fit firms that only need retrieval and analysis


The difference between Finch Legal and alternatives like Codes Health often comes down to service model philosophy. Finch Legal works as a comprehensive operations outsourcing partner, while Codes Health provides AI-powered medical intelligence that keeps operational control with your firm.


Codes Health is our featured pick. The other five are listed to help you compare service models, not ranked by independent testing.


## **1. Codes Health**


[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) goes beyond document collection to deliver organized, analyzed medical records that are ready for casework. It combines AI-powered analysis with human verification to support attorney and expert review, serving as a pre-litigation department for personal injury, mass tort, medical malpractice, workers' compensation, disability, insurance litigation, and wrongful death firms.


**Key Codes Health Advantages:**


-


**Retrieval in a couple of weeks** through multi-channel outreach across claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, patient portals, fax, email, and phone


-


**AI-assisted care review** that surfaces potential care concerns for attorney and qualified medical-expert assessment


-


**Missing-record detection** that helps teams identify gaps in treatment history before demand packages are finalized


-


**Medical summaries and chronologies** to support review of the underlying records


-


**Future medical expense extraction** identifying documented treatment recommendations and anticipated care


-


**Human-reviewed AI insights** to support case review


-


**Strategic Filevine partnership** with records, status updates, and communications embedded directly in case files


-


**Custom integrations** with CRM platforms and other medical software for high-volume firms


**Platform Capabilities:**


-


Medical, billing, and imaging record retrieval across provider types


-


AI-automated case chronologies organized by visit, with document summaries


-


Insights extraction identifying diagnoses, treatments, pre-existing conditions, and care events


-


Authorization validation before submission to help prevent rejections and delays


-


Persistent provider follow-up across calls, faxes, emails, and portals


-


HIPAA-compliant e-signature workflows for intake documents


**Catching Authorization Errors Before They Cost You Time:**


Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied record requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can send a request right back to the start. Under[HIPAA's right of access](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/guidance/access/index.html) , covered entities generally have 30 days to respond to patient requests, and state rules can vary, so a single rejection can add weeks to a case. Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.


**Why Plaintiff Firms Choose Codes Health:**


Firms handling medical-heavy litigation need more than fast document delivery. They need medical intelligence that strengthens case preparation. Codes Health's AI platform surfaces case-critical details like treatment gaps, missed appointments, and documented future care needs, then routes them for attorney review.


Codes Health offers flat-fee pricing. Contact Codes Health to confirm the services included, applicable provider charges, and terms for your firm's requests.


For Filevine users, the[Filevine partnership](https://www.filevine.com/news/filevine-partners-with-codes-health-to-bring-ai-native-medical-record-retrieval-to-legal-teams/) announced on July 13, 2026 cuts out the back-and-forth between retrieval portals and case management. You can request records, track status, message the Codes Health team, and receive completed files, all inside your existing Filevine project.


Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team keeps building out new workflows and products, so the platform continues to evolve, improve, and grow more comprehensive to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices.


## **2. LlamaLab**


LlamaLab focuses on rapid medical record retrieval and on finding treatment locations clients may not remember, using insurance claims data to surface additional providers.


**Platform Features:**


-


Vendor-reported four-day average retrieval, with some records available the same day


-


Provider discovery via claims data to identify treatment locations clients didn't list


-


Clinical qualification: LlamaLab advertises proof-of-injury review by a licensed clinical team in under seven days; confirm eligibility and when the timeline begins


-


Provider directory: LlamaLab advertises a directory containing more than four million healthcare entries


-


AI analysis included in its advertised plans


**Market Position:** LlamaLab's speed-first approach appeals to firms prioritizing rapid initial case evaluation, and its provider discovery feature can help in mass tort cases where plaintiffs have incomplete treatment recollection. As with any vendor, same-day availability does not establish that every requested record has been received. Ask which providers, date ranges, bills, and images are covered, how missing records are pursued, and what client participation is required.


**Pricing:** Plan-dependent pricing. LlamaLab advertises per-request and unlimited-request options. Confirm the applicable plan, setup fees, upload charges, and provider-cost coverage in a written quote.


**Best For:** Firms that prioritize fast initial case evaluation and provider discovery.


## **3. Tavrn**


Tavrn offers a platform covering intake, record retrieval, chronologies, and demand letter generation. The platform combines retrieval, chronologies, and demand-letter workflows. Confirm how each service is priced and packaged.


**Platform Features:**


-


Intake automation with case scoring capabilities


-


Medical record retrieval across provider networks


-


Medical chronologies generated from retrieved records


-


AI-generated demand letters based on case facts


-


REST API with webhooks for developer-friendly integrations


-


SOC 2 Type 1 and Type 2 reports available through its trust center, with a HIPAA BAA available on request


**Market Position:** Tavrn provides workflow breadth across multiple case stages. It connects with Litify, SmartAdvocate, Clio, and Smokeball through API integrations and webhook-based status updates, and advertises delivery into existing case systems.


**Pricing:** Tavrn currently describes per-request retrieval pricing in its official materials, with provider fees charged separately. Confirm current rates, included record types, and any separate charges for chronologies or demand letters directly with Tavrn.


**Best For:** Firms that want one platform from intake through demand letters.


## **4. National Record Retrieval**


National Record Retrieval provides managed medical record retrieval, case-management integrations, and record-review services for law firms.


**Platform Features:**

Managed record retrieval with provider follow-up


-


Flat-rate pricing for retrieval services


-


Medical chronologies, demand letters, and billing summaries


-


Integration support for platforms including Litify and Filevine


-


Nationwide coverage across all 50 states


**Market Position:** National Record Retrieval follows a staff-managed model in which experienced team members handle provider outreach, track request status, and compile returned documents. Its added review services give firms options beyond retrieval alone.


**Pricing:** Flat-rate pricing for retrieval; contact National Record Retrieval for current rates and review-service pricing.


**Best For:** Firms that prefer a staff-managed retrieval model with case-management integration support.


## **5. Ontellus**


Ontellus serves insurance carriers and high-volume law firms with enterprise infrastructure designed for large-scale record retrieval operations.


**Platform Features:**


-


High-volume processing for enterprise clients


-


Insurance carrier focus with claims-oriented workflows


-


AI-powered summaries and advanced analysis


-


Established compliance infrastructure for regulated industries


-


National provider network


**Market Position:** Ontellus focuses on operational efficiency for organizations processing large request volumes, with services built around dedicated records departments and established internal processes.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; contact Ontellus for a quote.


**Best For:** Large insurance defense operations or plaintiff firms with significant in-house litigation support resources.


## **6. Lexitas**


Lexitas provides bundled litigation services including record retrieval, court reporting, and trial support. With 40+ locations nationwide, it offers a single vendor across multiple service categories.


**Platform Features:**


-


Medical record retrieval as part of broader services


-


Record Insights, an AI-enabled medical chronology service


-


Court reporting and deposition services


-


Trial support including exhibits and presentations


-


eDiscovery and document management


**Market Position:** Lexitas suits firms that want retrieval, records review, and other litigation support under one roof. Lexitas advertises an average retrieval turnaround of 30 to 45 days. Confirm the expected timing for the providers and record types involved in your case.


**Pricing:** Contact Lexitas for current retrieval and Record Insights pricing.


**Best For:** Firms seeking one vendor across several litigation support categories.


## **Choosing the Right Medical Record Solution**


### **Comparing Analysis and Review Features**


Several alternatives offer medical summaries, chronologies, or AI-assisted analysis alongside retrieval. Compare the specific outputs, human-review process, source references, and separate charges rather than assuming that a retrieval provider delivers documents only. Codes Health pairs its AI analysis with human review and practice-area context built specifically for plaintiff litigation.


**What AI Medical Analysis Can Provide:**


-


Flags for potential breach-of-care indicators for attorney review


-


Treatment gap detection and missed appointment flags


-


Pre-existing condition documentation


-


Future medical expense extraction from physician recommendations


-


Organized summaries that support review of the underlying records


**Where General AI Falls Short:**


More firms are trying general-purpose AI tools like ChatGPT on medical records. These platforms aren't designed for litigation-grade medical record review, and they can miss details, misread medical terminology, or overlook patterns that matter in a case. Codes Health's AI platform is purpose-built to analyze medical records with high precision for legal use cases, with human review layered on top.


Whatever tool you consider, evaluate it using representative case files, checking factual accuracy, omissions, source traceability, and human-review procedures. A specialized workflow does not remove the need to verify findings.


### **Complete Records vs. Fast Partial Records**


Speed metrics need context. Same-day availability does not establish that every requested record has been received. Codes Health's position is that services offering same-day retrieval often deliver only the records that are immediately available rather than the complete set. Filling the remaining gaps typically requires client involvement, which can frustrate clients and contribute to churn. Codes Health works toward complete records in weeks, not months.


Complete medical record retrieval requires:


-


Direct provider outreach through multiple channels


-


Persistent follow-up until records are delivered


-


Completeness verification against original requests


-


Gap identification for missing facilities or date ranges


Codes Health advertises retrieval in a couple of weeks and checks returned records for completeness. Actual timing and availability depend on the providers, authorizations, and records requested. Checking returned records against the request can help teams identify outstanding documentation before demand preparation.


### **Integration Depth Matters**


For firms using case management platforms, integration depth affects day-to-day efficiency. Surface-level integrations can mean manual data transfer, while deeper integrations embed retrieval workflows directly into case files. Codes Health offers an embedded Filevine workflow. Other providers also support case-management integrations or work directly in a firm's existing system, so compare request submission, status updates, communications, and document delivery.


**Codes Health Filevine Integration:**


-


Submit requests directly from Filevine projects


-


Track status and provider outreach in real time


-


Communicate with the Codes Health team within case workflows


-


Receive completed records delivered into your case file


-


Review retrieval history without switching platforms


For high-volume firms using other systems, Codes Health builds[custom integrations](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) with CRM platforms and other medical software to keep your workflow connected across your technology stack.

The result is complete records in weeks, not months, without giving up control of your cases. If your current process still involves chasing providers, re-submitting rejected requests, or discovering gaps during demand prep, Codes Health is the alternative built to fix that.
